gap:logistic_regression_analysis.statement: Need to fit logistic regression models with specific gradient descent conventions and analyze: (1) optimal L2 regularization via 5-fold CV, (2) interaction feature utility via paired t-test, (3) best model compression configuration.

hyp:interaction_features_marginal.statement: Interaction features (x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3) likely provide marginal improvement in Brier score; paired t-test will determine if t-statistic exceeds 2.0 threshold.

claim:q1_best_lambda.statement: Through 5-fold cross-validated Brier score optimization, lambda=0.1 provides the lowest mean cross-validated Brier score (0.207077) compared to alternatives [0.0, 0.01, 1.0, 10.0], with an improvement of 0.0089 over the unregularized baseline (lambda=0.0).

claim:q2_interaction_features.statement: Interaction features (x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3) significantly improve model performance. Paired t-test comparing base model versus interaction-augmented model across 5 folds yields t-statistic of 4.374 (p-value < 0.05), exceeding the threshold of 2.0, indicating interaction features provide statistically significant improvement in Brier score.

claim:q3_best_compression.statement: Among tested model compression configurations, sparsity20_bits4 achieves the highest retention ratio of 0.9992, meaning compressed model performance (Brier=0.141873) is nearly identical to dense model (Brier=0.141762), making it the optimal compression configuration.
